correctness.rationale: The exact uniqueness condition S intersects N\M for every distinct perfect matching N is a theorem by direct survival equivalence. Two stand-alone standard-library programs exhaust every perfect matching (36), every potential smaller deletion subset and minimum witness, with independent graph presentations; the LCF isomorphism is explicitly checked. The first proves 120 automorphisms and two orbits of 30 and six; the second checks every one of 36 matchings, returning identical 30/6 ordinary (4,8)/(5,22) and independent-edge (8,4)/(8,5) profiles. Scripts and exact outputs are embedded; no infinite inference is made.

originality.rationale: The earliest cited 2014 paper defines fixed-matching anti-forcing; the 2015 fullerene theorem already proves min>=4, C20 min=4 and nonmatching shape of 4-edge witnesses. Critically, Han–Zhou–Wang 2023 already gives C20 ordinary anti-forcing spectrum [4,5]; it is excluded from the novelty claim. The claim instead gives 30/6 orbit multiplicities, complete minimum-witness multiplicities and the sharp disjoint-edge deletion size 8 for all matchings, including its multiplicities. Relevant known general results and published matching-complex results do not state or logically imply these exact numbers. Unindexed publications and 2023 unpublished underlying computation are residual risks.

value.rationale: In the smallest fullerene, edge deletions rigidify a chosen Kekulé structure; forbidding incident deletions is a natural constrained-observation/edge-attack rule. Existing general bounds only rule out size-four disjoint certificates, whereas the exact optimum eight for every perfect matching is a sharp and substantial 3–4-edge penalty. Complete automorphism-stratified minimum-witness counts provide a motivated fine anti-forcing invariant and useful finite benchmark. No large-family/general theorem is claimed.
